description:
In relay_client.rs, read_line uses 'line.len() > MAX_SMTP_LINE' (accepts up to 512 bytes, the RFC maximum) with an explicit comment: 'Use > (not >=) to accept the maximum valid length.' But parse_smtp_line immediately uses '>= MAX_SMTP_LINE', so a 512-byte reply line—which is RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1.5 compliant—is accepted by the I/O guard and then rejected by the parser with ProtocolError. The result is spurious connection failures against servers that send maximally-sized SMTP reply lines. The test 'parse_smtp_line_exactly_512_bytes_is_rejected' codifies this incorrect behavior as expected, which means the test is validating the bug rather than the spec.

## Context
relay_client.rs line 733 uses >, line 775 uses >=. RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1.5: max reply line length is 512 octets INCLUDING CRLF. A 512-byte line (including CRLF) is legal.
title: relay_client: parse_smtp_line rejects RFC-valid 512-byte reply lines
